metadata.title: Mortgage Rates, New Homes and Building Jobs

events.label: Housing starts peak at 2.27 million a year
Starts down 41%, but trade jobs still at their peak
Mortgage rates hit a record low of 2.68%
Mortgage rates near 7%; buyers pull back

explanation.summary: The three cards show a chain: the 30-year mortgage rate, how many new homes builders start, and how many people work in building trades (plumbers, electricians, roofers). The stripes below show every month since 1996: red means higher than a year before, blue means lower. Rates give home building only a weak push. But once homes are started, building jobs follow strongly, about a year later, because workers are still finishing homes already begun.
explanation.methodology: 30-year fixed mortgage rate from Freddie Mac via FRED (weekly, averaged by month). Housing starts are Census Bureau new privately-owned units started (via FRED, seasonally adjusted annual rate). Specialty trade contractor jobs are from the BLS Current Employment Statistics (CES2023800001).

key_findings.title: January 2006: The Building Peak
key_findings.description: Builders started homes at a pace of 2.27 million a year, the highest on the chart. By April 2009 that pace had collapsed to 478,000, a fall of 79%.
key_findings.significance: The housing bubble and its bust in one line.

key_findings.title: August 2007: Trade Jobs Peak Late
key_findings.description: New starts were already down 41% from their peak, yet specialty trade jobs hit their bubble-era high of 4.84 million. Then they fell for five years, to 3.52 million in July 2012.
key_findings.significance: Construction jobs lag home starts by many months, so they are a slow signal, not an early one.

key_findings.title: December 2020: Record-Low Mortgage Rates
key_findings.description: Mortgage rates fell to 2.68%. Starts jumped back above 1.6 million a year. When rates rose to about 7% in late 2022, starts cooled again.
key_findings.significance: Cheap money brings buyers and builders back quickly. As of 2026, trade jobs are at a record 5.28 million.
